title: Apple MLX — SyncToMLX and forward
why: Run a Go Dense layer on Apple MLX GPU with an explicit SyncToMLX lifetime — forward-only, no Mount/TrainMSE twin.
what: Install welvet.mlx, SyncToMLX an identity Dense, set BackendMLX, and forward a Float32 tensor.
body_extra:
User-owned sync

MLX does not use nativemetal.Mount. Weights stay in Go Stores until you call SyncToMLX (caps-check + capture). Then set Exec.Backend = core.BackendMLX (or use core.PreferMLX() when the dylib + Metal GPU are ready) and call the ordinary layer Forward.

must(layer.SyncToMLX())
layer.Exec.Backend = core.BackendMLX
_, post, err := dense.Forward(layer, x)

Requirements and honesty

Go Welvet v1.7.0 adds the independent welvet.mlx 1.0.0 library at github.com/openfluke/welvet.mlx. Install into the Go tree:

cd ../welvet.mlx
./scripts/macos_install_go.sh

Needs Apple silicon macOS, cgo, shipped libwelvet_mlx.dylib, and a Metal GPU. nativemlx.Available() is false without Metal — there is no CPU fallback labeled as MLX and no silent fallthrough to welvet.metal. Other hosts print SKIP.

Forward-only: no TrainMSE / NormalBP / SyncToGo train loop on MLX. SyncFromMLX exists for API symmetry (mirror → Go) but forward does not mutate W. Caps reject unsupported layer×dtype mounts.

Sibling contract: docs/MLX_ONLY.md. Caps tour: §111. Dense + Sequential: §112. Live matrices: §113. Metal train twin remains §82–88.

title: Apple MLX — caps and dtype rejects
why: Unsupported mounts must hard-fail before any GPU work — not soft-fallback to Go labeled as MLX.
what: Print SupportedLayers, accept dense/float32, and show RequireLayer rejecting dense/float64.
body_extra:
Caps table

nativemlx.LayerSupported(layer, dtype) and SupportedLayers() mirror the welvet.mlx C ABI caps. SyncToMLX / RequireLayer refuse anything outside that table. Dense GPU compute rejects float64; host I/O stays Float32 activations with FormatNone parameter storage.

welvet.mlx 1.0.0 caps list the signed leaf ops (Dense, Softmax, RMSNorm, LayerNorm, CNN2/3, ConvT2/3, LSTM, Embedding, Residual, SwiGLU, MHA). Sequential is a container that mounts supported children — see §112. Full dtype matrix: FORWARD_CHECKLIST.md.

title: Apple MLX — Dense prepare and Sequential
why: Show prepare-once Dense execute and a small Sequential tower on the same MLX session.
what: SyncToMLX a Dense with PrepareMLX, then SyncToMLX a two-Dense Sequential and forward once.
body_extra:
Prepare vs online

Dense can PrepareMLX(batch) outside the timed loop so repeated Forward calls stay execute-only. Sequential rebuilds a welvet.mlx Sequential from supported children (Dense / Softmax / RMSNorm / LayerNorm today) and host-ping-pongs child MLX evals.

These shapes are API demos — not performance claims. Live large-shape matrices live in w2a go_v_mlx (§113).

title: Apple MLX — go_v_mlx results pointers
why: Find the sibling harness and live MLX parity matrices after the small usage chapters.
what: Print Go v1.7.0 / welvet.mlx 1.0.0 pins and commands for w2a go_v_mlx. No GPU required.
body_extra:
Where live results live

This chapter is host-only. It does not claim timings from loading the page. Sibling MLX engine: github.com/openfluke/welvet.mlx. Suite README: w2a/suites/go_v_mlx.

cd ../../w2a && go test ./tests/go_v_mlx -count=1 -timeout 60m
cd ../../welvet.mlx && ./scripts/macos_install_go.sh
cd welvet/examples && ./run_mlx.sh

Engine pin: welvet.mlx 1.0.0, Go binding nativemlx (Welvet v1.7.0). Platform: Apple silicon macOS for SyncToMLX / BackendMLX. Pure-MLX contract: no silent CPU path labeled MLX; no TrainMSE on MLX.
